title: A maintenance request bounces between resident, manager and vendor until the resident loses trust
job: Resolve resident maintenance issues quickly with clear ownership, priority and follow-through.
surfaceComplaint: The resident keeps asking for updates and we keep chasing the vendor.
mechanism: Requests often lack diagnostic context, ownership moves across teams/vendors, and status updates are decoupled from actual completion. Coordination labor fills the gaps.

workflow.friction: closed work order may not mean solved

economics.painCostNote: Maintenance affects both operating cost and renewal/retention.

buyer.roiLogic: Maintenance touches every unit and affects renewals.

distribution.acquisition: Prove triage/closure gains on exported history before integration.

competitors.gap: semantic triage and verified closure may remain weak
does not solve owner/resident communication state

intervention.notBuildYet: No autonomous dispatch for safety-critical issues.

experiment.artifactRequest: request text/photos + assignment + timestamps + reopen status
experiment.success: ≥25% fewer manager touches and ≥20% lower reopen rate or faster resolution
experiment.kill: existing PMS solves it or real constraint is vendor supply only

claims.text: Buildium's 2026 industry report says 56% of owners cite maintenance support as the main reason they hired a property manager and as their #1 stress source.
Buildium's renters report says maintenance is the leading driver of renter satisfaction and follow-through is a major gap.
Verified closure is a distinct problem from work-order creation.
